title: Rakuen Tsuihō -Expelled from Paradise- Kokoro no Resonance Anime Film Opens in Taiwan on November 20
content:
MediaLink International announced on Monday that it will open Rakuen Tsuihō -Expelled from Paradise- Kokoro no Resonance (Heart's Resonance), the all-new feature-length anime film sequel to the Expelled from Paradise film, in Taiwan on November 20.

MediaLink International will also screen the first Expelled from Paradise film in 4K in Taiwan on November 6.

Rakuen Tsuihō -Expelled from Paradise- Kokoro no Resonance will open in Japan on November 13. The franchise is also spawning a new game titled Expelled from Paradise -The Stellar Angel- ( Rakuen Tsuihō -The Stellar Angel- ) with an original story that will launch on November 26 for Nintendo Switch and PC via Steam .

While the original announcement of the film had featured the title Rakuen Tsuihō : Libera ted from Paradise , a later announcement listed the title as Rakuen Tsuihō -Expelled from Paradise- Kokoro no Resonance as well as Rakuen Tsuihō: Kokoro no Resonance instead.

The cast members are:

• Ayane Sakura as Gabriel

• Saori Hayami as Alma

• Yoshino Aoyama as Danel

• Sally Amaki as Raguel

• Sumire Morohoshi as Penem

Rie Kugimiya reprises her role as Angela Balzac in the film.

The film reunites the main staff of Expelled from Paradise , including director Seiji Mizushima , scriptwriter Gen Urobuchi of Nitroplus , character designer Masatsugu Saitō , and composer NARASAKI . Toei Animation is producing the animation.

The other staff members include:

• Mechanical Designers: Kanetake Ebikawa, Junya Ishigaki, Takayuki Yanase

• Animation Supervisor: Naoki Ogita

• Modeling Supervisor: Kento Kume

• Mecha Modeling Lead: Toyokazu Hashimoto

• Producer: Kōichi Ioguchn

Expelled from Paradise debuted in 13 theaters in Japan in November 2014, and sold 110,000 tickets. The film's Blu-ray Disc and DVD release in Japan sold more than 70,000 copies. The film won the Best Animation of the Year Award at the 24th Japan Movie Critics Awards in May 2015.

The film returned to theaters in Japan in November 2024 in 4K resolution as Expelled from Paradise -Impelled by 10th Anniversary- to commemorate the film's 10-year anniversary.
author: ANN

title: QCinema Film Festival Screens We Are Aliens, Perfect Blue Anime Films
content:
The festival will screen films at Gateway Cineplex 18, Robinsons Galleria, TriNoma, Fisher Box Office, and SM City Fairview from November 13 to 22.

Kōhei Kadowaki and NOTHING NEW 's We Are Aliens ( Ware Ware wa Uchūjin ) anime film

centers on Tsubasa and Gyōtarō, two boys who as elementary school students became close friends, but jealousy and misunderstandings eventually drove them apart. Years have passed and the two boys have gone in different directions in life. But when the memories from their past come back, they must face what happened between them years ago.

The film stars Ryōta Bandō ( Fureru. , live-action How to Train Your Dragon's Japanese dub ) as Tsubasa, and Amane Okayama ( Blue Giant , live-action I’’s , Hirayasumi ) as Gyōtarō, when both characters are young adults. Child actors Yūto Maki and Tasuku Nakagome — who were both selected through auditions — voice Tsubasa and Gyōtarō, respectively, when they were younger. Other cast members include Sakurazaka46 idol group member Ten Yamasaki as Konatsu, comedian Kemuri Matsui as Batahara, Gaku Sano as Tsubasa's friend Seiya Toda, Reika Ōzeki as young Seiya, Arisa Sasaki as Toda's friend Elmo Matsushita, and Edo Harumi as a calligraphy teacher.

We Are Aliens opened in Japan on September 15. The film screened at the Directors' Fortnight of the Cannes Film Festival on May 14, and screened in competition at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival, which ran from June 21 to 27. The Melbourne International Film Festival (MIFF), the New Zealand International Film Festival (NZIFF), and the "Japanese Animation Special: Masterpieces of Madness, Exhilarating Prospects 12+1" category of the 31st Busan International Film Festival (BIFF) also screened the film. Ottawa International Animation Festival awarded the film the Grand Prize for Animated Feature last month.

Kadowaki, who created the second BEASTARS season's ending sequence and music videos for YOASOBI , served as the film's planner, scriptwriter, director, storyboard artist, and editor. Yaffle — who previously produced music for Fujii Kaze, Kenshi Yonezu , and others — composed the music. NOTHING NEW planned and produced the film, and French studio Miyu Productions ( Ghost Cat Anzu , A New Dawn ) collaborated on the production, after joining on the project in June 2025. Artist adieu performs the film's theme song "Sasakure" (Split).

Kon based his Perfect Blue anime film on Yoshikazu Takeuchi 's Perfect Blue: Complete Metamorphosis novel.
author: ANN

title: Sailor Moon S1 UK Steelbook Blu-ray Released on Monday
content:
Based on the manga by Naoko Takeuchi , Sailor Moon was adapted as a 200-part TV series in Japan, running from 1992 to 1997.

My Gift Lvl 9999 Unlimited Gacha was made by J.C. Staff in 2025 and is about a powerful Level 999 Overlord . The story is described on Amazon as follows:

" After being recruited to join the Concord of Tribes, a group consisting of one each of the other eight races, Light was shocked when they suddenly attempted to kill him! Miraculously managing to escape and survive in the deepest depths of a dungeon. Light is astonished to learn that he's much more powerful than anyone imagined and his thoughts quickly turn to revenge. It won't be easy, and it may take years, but with the aid of his newly summoned Ever-Seeking Maid and his increased abilities, he'll cut a bloody path through their dead and dying bodies!"

"When Jinta defeats a powerful demon, he gains its power but also a terrible prophecy, one that will shatter his adopted family and leave him wandering the lands in search of resolution. The shrine maiden he'd sworn to protect is dead and her killer missing, he changes his name and travels Japan in search of his missing sister and the foretold destiny he dreads but must seek. How many miles must he journey? How many years will it take? As the decades pass he becomes a legend, helping those in need along the way as he marches toward his fate in Sword of the Demon Hunter !"

"On their way to settle things with Raphtalia's ancestral homeland, Naofumi's party travels through Siltvelt, where the Shield Hero is worshiped. But when the nation tries to keep him there, Naofumi is caught between rival factions vying for power."

"Roger and Whitebeard face off, and Oden joins Roger's journey to the island at the end of the Grand Line. Returning to the Land of Wano, Oden discovers Orcochi's treachery and makes the ultimate sacrifice to save his country. Back in the present time, Kin'emon and his samurai begin the raid on Onigashima, only to learn their plan was leaked. The Sunny joins the fight, but a spy kidnaps Momonosuke!"
author: ANN

title: 'Sony YAY!' Airs New Episodes of Shin-chan TV Anime in India on November 2
content:
The channel aired Eiga Crayon Shin-chan: Ora-tachi no Kyōryū Nikki ( Shin chan Our Dinosaur Diary ), the Crayon Shin-chan franchise 's 31st 2D animated film , in India in October 2025. The film premiered in Japan in August 2024.

Eiga Crayon Shin-chan Chō Karei! Shakunetsu no Kasukabe Dancers (Crayon Shin-chan the Movie: Super Magnificent! Scorching Kasukabe Dancers), the 32nd 2D anime film in the Crayon Shin-chan series, opened in Japan in August 2025. It opened in India in September 2025. The film is the "series' first dance entertainment movie" and the series' first film set in India.

Eiga Crayon Shin-chan Kikikaikai! Ora no Yōkai Bake-shon ( Crayon Shin-chan The Movie Super Strange! My Yōkai Monster Vacation), the 33rd 2D anime film in the Crayon Shin-chan series, opened in Japan on July 31.

title: Bleach Surprises With First Episode Remake in Anime Finale – Watch Now
content:
Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War has now come to an end with its final episode, and the anime went back 22 years with a special remake of one of the biggest moments from its very first episode. Bleach fans had been waiting for over a decade from the end of Tite Kubo’s original manga series to see the final arc make its proper anime adaptation debut. And the final season of the series really went all out to make the anime version of the finale the most complete take on the story yet.

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War’ s final episode picks up ten years after the end of the fight against Yhwach , and with it the anime gave Ichigo and Rukia one last moment to reflect on their journey after all this time. Thinking back to when the two of them first met, the final episode of the anime offers a surprising remake of this classic moment with a classic theme song backing it all up as well. You can check it out below as shared by Viz Media.

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War Finale Remakes Ichigo & Rukia’s First Meeting

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War Episode 50 gives fans a look at Ichigo and Rukia’s lives ten years after the end of the fight with Yhwach, and with it Ichigo and Rukia get to have a fun reunion. Rukia has been named the new Captain of Squad 13 and has had a child together with Renji, and Ichigo has gone on to marry Orihime to have a child of their own. But upon this reunion, the two of them take a brief moment to reflect on their long journey thus far to where they are now.

The episode then goes the extra mile by not only revealing the flashback of Ichigo and Rukia’s first real meeting with one another, but fully remakes it within the modern Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War style. It even has the classic version of the “Number One” insert theme as heard in the original TV series (as it was changed for the new era of the anime), and ends with a montage of all of Ichigo’s biggest moments . It’s a full circle moment for Ichigo as the Bleach anime comes to an end.

Is Bleach ‘s Anime Really Over?

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War has now ended its TV anime run after four seasons, and it’s 22 years after the original Bleach anime began its own run. It had been unfortunately cancelled before the anime ever got to adapt the final arc for Kubo’s manga, and it had taken nearly 20 years to get any word on a potential return. But fans of the series never lost hope that the anime would come back someday, and that faith was rewarded with a successful comeback.

It’s been a huge comeback in turn too as Bleach ‘s manga not only returned for a special one-shot for its 20th anniversary two years ago, a special remake of more of these classic moments around that time, a spinoff series, and now the franchise is currently readying for the release of a new mobile game and more. With a major event teasing more of what’s to come hitting next year , it might not totally be the end of Bleach just yet. What are you hoping to see from Bleach in the future? Let us know your thoughts in the comments!

title: Demon Slayer Studio’s Next Big Movie Hypes Crunchyroll U.S. Release – Watch New Trailer
content:
Witch on the Holy Night is the next big movie coming from the same studio behind Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba Infinity Castle , and Crunchyroll is gearing up for its release across the United States with a slick new trailer showing it off. Studio Ufotable has made a major name for itself with its work on the Demon Slayer TV anime and film releases, but it’s really gotten started even earlier with lots of projects adapting various TYPE-MOON stories . Now a new one is heading to theaters soon.

Witch on the Holy Night is the next major TYPE-Moon franchise coming to life through Studio Ufotable, and it’s going to be hitting theaters across Japan this November. But it won’t be too much longer before it comes to the United States and other territories in January . To better prepare fans for its release, Crunchyroll has dropped a cool new trailer for Witch on the Holy Night that you can check out in the video below.

When Does Witch on the Holy Night Come Out in the U.S.?

Witch on the Holy Night will be first making its debut in Japan on November 20th, and Crunchyroll and Sony Pictures Entertainment will then be releasing the new film in the United States, Canada and more international territories on January 29th next yea r with both Japanese and English dubbed audio planned. Based off of the TYPE-MOON visual novel from Kinoko Nasu, the film is directed by Masashi Takeuchi for ufotable with Moe Tsuzuki providing the character designs, Manabu Kamino handling the editing, and Hideyuki Fukasawa composing the music.

The Japanese voice cast for Witch on the Holy Night will be reprising the roles from TYPE-MOON’s original visual novel release and they include Haruka Tomatsu as Aoko Aozaki, Kana Hanazawa as Alice Kuonji, and Yusuke Kobayashi as Soujyuro Shizuki. The English dub voice cast for the film has yet to be revealed as of this time, however, but we’ll likely get an update on that closer to its release with further teases for the English dub. This trailer also reveals the film’s theme song titled “Yoru to Ao” as performed by supercell too.

What’s So Special About Witch on the Holy Night ?

Witch on the Holy Night is within TYPE-MOON’s extended universe of Fate/stay night related projects . Although it’s not directly connected to that universe of prequel visual novel releases and anime adaptations, it serves as a prequel to Tsukihime (which has already had its own anime outing) from the same writer behind it all, Kinoko Nasu. Now that this project is finally making its own proper anime due, it’s yet another major entry in TYPE-MOON’s anime universe through Studio Ufotable.

Witch on the Holy Night’ s upcoming release is even more exciting because it will presumably free up Studio Ufotable to start talking about their next major entry in the Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba Infinity Castle trilogy . No release window or date has been revealed for the follow up to the massively popular first film as of this time, but we could see even more of it after this film finally hits. How are you liking the look of Witch on the Holy Night so far? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Welcome to Demon School Iruma-kun Confirms New Spinoff Release Date With First Look
content:
Welcome to Demon School, Iruma-kun is coming back with a new spinoff anime next year, and the series has now confirmed its release date with the first real look at its alternate universe makeovers for fan favorite characters. The anime adaptation for Osamu Nishi’s Welcome to Demon School, Iruma-kun has been a breath of fresh air for its four season run thus far , but there’s even more of it on the way. With that fourth season ending earlier this year, the anime is coming back with a spinoff in 2027.

It’s just going to look totally different than anything that fans had seen in action with the original TV anime series . Welcome to Demon School, Iruma-kun: IruMafia Edition is an official spinoff of the main series that’s set in an alternate world where Iruma is not adopted and taken into a fun school life like in the original, but is thrown into the mafia underworld instead. Making its debut next January, you can check out the new poster for the Iruma-kun spinoff anime below.

Welcome to Demon School, Iruma-kun: IruMafia Edition Confirms January 2027 Release Date

Welcome to Demon School, Iruma-kun: IruMafia Edition is currently scheduled to make its debut in Japan on January 4th as part of the Winter 2027 anime schedule kicking off the next year of new anime releases. No international release platform plans have yet to be revealed as of this time, but it’s been confirmed that the debut outing for the spinoff anime series will be running for 12 episodes with its broadcast on NHK in Japan. The production staff and voice cast for the new anime has revealed its first few new additions to the fray as well.

Welcome to Demon School, Iruma-kun: IruMafia Edition will be directed by Keiichiro Kawaguchi for Tatsunoko Production with Kazuyuki Fudeyasu handling the series composition, Kenji Fujisaki providing the character designs, and Yayoi Sekimukai composing the music. The voice cast from the main series will be returning for their alternate universe selves too with Ayumu Murase as Iruma, Ryohei Kimura as Alice Asmodeus, Ayaka Asai as Clara Valac, Mitsuki Saiga as Opera, Saori Hayami as Ameri, and Daisuke Ono as Kalego Naberius. But they’re all going to be much different than in the main series.

What to Know for Welcome to Demon School, Iruma-kun: IruMafia Edition

Welcome to Demon School, Iruma-kun: IruMafia Edition is an alternate universe version of the main story from Hiroja, overseen by original series creator Osamu Nishi. After helping Sullivan (who in the spinoff is the Don of a Mafia instead), Iruma is quickly recruited into a new gang life surrounded by familiar faces with edgier personalities than fans might recognize. With it kicking off the new year, it’s not going to be too much longer before fans get to see the anime in motion.

As for the main Welcome to Demon School, Iruma-kun anime franchise, following the end of the fourth season it was announced to now be working on a feature film production next . No release window or date has been revealed for the anime’s movie debut as of this time, but you can catch up with all four seasons of the original TV anime now streaming with Crunchyroll in the meantime. Are you excited for this new Welcome to Demon School, Iruma-kun spinoff? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

The anime adaptation for Osamu Nishi’s Welcome to Demon School, Iruma-kun has been a breath of fresh air for its four season run thus far , but there’s even more of it on the way. With that fourth season ending earlier this year, the anime is coming back with a spinoff in 2027.

It’s just going to look totally different than anything that fans had seen in action with the original TV anime series . Welcome to Demon School, Iruma-kun: IruMafia Edition is an official spinoff of the main series that’s set in an alternate world where Iruma is not adopted and taken into a fun school life like in the original, but is thrown into the mafia underworld instead. Making its debut next January, you can check out the new poster for the Iruma-kun spinoff anime below.
Welcome to Demon School, Iruma-kun: IruMafia Edition Confirms January 2027 Release Date

Welcome to Demon School, Iruma-kun: IruMafia Edition is currently scheduled to make its debut in Japan on January 4th as part of the Winter 2027 anime schedule kicking off the next year of new anime releases. No international release platform plans have yet to be revealed as of this time, but it’s been confirmed that the debut outing for the spinoff anime series will be running for 12 episodes with its broadcast on NHK in Japan. The production staff and voice cast for the new anime has revealed its first few new additions to the fray as well.

Welcome to Demon School, Iruma-kun: IruMafia Edition will be directed by Keiichiro Kawaguchi for Tatsunoko Production with Kazuyuki Fudeyasu handling the series composition, Kenji Fujisaki providing the character designs, and Yayoi Sekimukai composing the music. The voice cast from the main series will be returning for their alternate universe selves too with Ayumu Murase as Iruma, Ryohei Kimura as Alice Asmodeus, Ayaka Asai as Clara Valac, Mitsuki Saiga as Opera, Saori Hayami as Ameri, and Daisuke Ono as Kalego Naberius. But they’re all going to be much different than in the main series.

Welcome to Demon School, Iruma-kun: IruMafia Edition is an alternate universe version of the main story from Hiroja, overseen by original series creator Osamu Nishi. After helping Sullivan (who in the spinoff is the Don of a Mafia instead), Iruma is quickly recruited into a new gang life surrounded by familiar faces with edgier personalities than fans might recognize. With it kicking off the new year, it’s not going to be too much longer before fans get to see the anime in motion.

title: Detective Conan Anime's 4th Collection of Episodes 'Clash of the Red and Black' Streams on Crunchyroll, Netflix on November 1
content:
Netflix had previously teased episodes for November 1.

TMS began streaming the first specially curated selection of Detective Conan episodes in July 2025 on Netflix and Crunchyroll . The episodes are streaming in Japanese and with a new English dub by Studio Nano , different from the Bang Zoom! and Funimation dubs. The first selection of episodes is titled "Conan vs. The Black Organization" and features episodes with the titular antagonists, including ones that had never before been available in the U.S. Crunchyroll and Netflix added more episodes to the first collection in August 2025. "Rivals of the Great Detective," the second curated collection featuring episdoes related to Conan's rivals and allies, began streaming in November 2025, and added more episodes on January 1. The third selection "FBI Intervention" began streaming on May 1, and continued with more episodes on August 1.

Gōshō Aoyama launched the manga in Shogakukan 's Weekly Shounen Sunday magazine in 1994. The manga has spawned a television anime that has been running since January 1996, as well as an accompanying anime film series. Viz Media publishes the manga under the name Case Closed , Funimation 's original localized title. The English manga release uses the same English names from the original Funimation dub when applicable, and it uses the original Japanese names otherwise.

The manga series centers on Conan Edogawa, the alias of detective Shinichi Kudo, whose body shrunk after being poisoned at the beginning of the story. Together with detective Kogoro Mori and his daughter Ran, Conan helps the police solve difficult mysteries.

title: Tetsuya Chiba, Ashita no Joe’s Legendary Creator, Dies at 87
content:
Tetsuya Chiba, the legendary creator behind manga hits such as Ashita no Joe and more, has died at the age of 87. Kodansha has announced that the legendary creator had passed away on October 22nd at the age of 87 due to myelodysplastic syndrome, disorders that impact bone marrow, at a hospital in Tokyo. A private funeral service with family in attendance has since been held. Chiba is one of the most notable creators to ever hit the scene in Japan, and was even one of the rarely recognized for his impact on manga.

Chiba was awarded the Order of Culture award in Japan to commemorate his outstanding contributions to developing Japanese culture in 2024, and was one of the very few manga artists who have ever won the prestigious award. Born in 1939, Chiba has been widely regarded for his sports manga stories across various magazines and had even been releasing new chapters of his latest work, Hinemosu Notari Nikki , before going on a hiatus earlier this September.

RIP Tetsuya Chiba (1939-2026)

Tetsuya Chiba’s first real breakout is likely the one that fans in the West know fully well for themselves. Ashita no Joe (otherwise known as Tomorrow’s Joe with its initial English license) was written by Asao Takamori with Chiba providing the art. Making its debut with Kodansha’s Weekly Shonen Magazine in 1968, the series ran until 1973 and is often held in high regard as one of the most influential boxing series of all time. The series followed a kid down on his luck and steadily rising through the ranks as one of Japan’s top boxers. In fact, the series was such a big deal in Japan, one character’s death actually sparked a real life funeral with lots of fans in attendance.

The series went on to be adapted into a TV anime series, live-action feature films, and more as Chiba continued his illustrious career with other works in the years that followed such as I’m Teppei, Notari Matsutaro, Ashita Tenki ni Naare and more. Chiba has been such a notable creator and artist through the decades that he’s received many huge awards such as Order of the Rising Sun, Gold Rays with Rosette, and was named a Person of Cultural Merit and more. Kodansha even named a special award for him to give out to other up and coming creators, The Tetsuya Chiba Award.

Kodansha shared the following statement about Chiba’s passing, “Tetsuya Chiba, who left us numerous masterpieces over his 70-year career as an artist, possessed endless love and trust in the creative medium of manga,” the statement begins. ‘”The Tetsuya Chiba Award,’ our company’s award for new talent, has been running for an impressive 46 years since its establishment. Informed by Chiba-sensei’s words, many new manga artists took their first steps toward becoming professionals and continue to be active today. Chiba-sensei’s enormous contribution to the manga world was irreplaceable.”

There are few creators that have been able to have as big of an impact as Chiba has had on the world, and the artist leaves behind a history and body of work that is going to continue to inspire many others for decades to come. ComicBook extends our condolences to Tetsuya Chiba’s family, friends and loves ones in this tough time.

title: GKIDS Releases cocoon Wartime Anime Digitally With Blu-ray Disc Release Shipping on January 19
content:
GKIDS announced on Tuesday that it has released cocoon – One Summer of Girlhood ( cocoon Aru Natsu no Shōjo-tachi Yori ), the anime of Machiko Kyō 's Cocoon manga, digitally on Apple TV and Prime Video. The company will release the anime on Blu-ray Disc on January 19.

This year's JAPAN CUTS event screened the anime's North American premiere on July 10. The 30th annual Fantasia International Film Festival is screening the Canadian premiere.

The anime debuted on BS- NHK in March 2025, before airing on NHK General that August.

The anime stars Hikari Mitsushima as Mayu and Marika Itō as San.

Yukimitsu Ina (animation director for Tatami Time Machine Blues ) directed the anime, and kensuke ushio ( A Silent Voice , Chainsaw Man , DAN DA DAN ) composed the music. Hitomi Tateno , a veteran Studio Ghibli animator, was the animation producer, with the studio Sasayuri producing the anime.

The manga is set in a tropical southern island, and centers on San and her best friend Mayu, who go to the island's top all-girls school. War soon comes to their country, and the students of the school soon become embroiled in the war effort, and soon enough, the rear-line care of the wounded. One by one, San and Mayu lose their friends in the ever-worsening war.

Kyō released the manga in 2010, 65 years after the end of World War II. The anime's 2025 release came 80 years after the end of World War II.

Viz Media licensed the manga.

Kyō published the Mitsuami no Kami-sama manga in Shueisha 's now- defunct Jump X ( Jump Kai ) magazine in 2013, and Shueisha published the manga's first and only compiled book volume in the same year. The manga won an award in the 18th Annual Osamu Tezuka Cultural Prize in March 2014. The manga inspired Production I.G 's Pigtails 28-minute short anime film. The short made its international debut in April 2016 at the WorldFest Houston International Film Festival, where it won the Platinum Remi Award in the Classic Cel Animation Category. Pigtails has won multiple awards, including the Diamond Award in the Animated Film category at the 2016 California Film Awards.
